content:
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- Model consistently under-estimates price spikes in the 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5 price point buffer after a sentiment spike (≥0.67) in the prior 5–7 days.
- Model over-estimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; reduce first 3–5 days’ forecast by 0.5–1.0 price point.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >1.5σ above recent 18-day mean, reduce by 0.5–1.0 price point; if <1.5σ below, increase by 0.5–1.0.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often lag by 1–3 days; if sentiment is trending, add 0.3–0.7 price point offset to align with sentiment momentum.
